ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
test_cases_present: partial — ADIv5 / ARM IHI 0031C defines the architectural rules, the 46-bit transaction format, mandatory DP/AP register sets, and the SWJ-DP mode-switching mechanism, but does not provide a formal verification testbench. The categories below are spec-derived compliance scenarios that any ADIv5-conformant SW-DP / SWJ-DP / MEM-AP must pass.
derived_compliance_test_categories: Line reset — drive ≥ 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH from each possible internal state; verify SW-DP wire-level FSM returns to Idle, SELECT and CTRL/STAT clear, posted-read queue drained.
IDCODE/DPIDR readback — issue Request(APnDP=0, RnW=1, A[2:3]=0); verify ACK=OK and 32-bit response matches the mask-fixed DPIDR value with bit 0 = 1 (RAO).
Request packet parity — issue Request with deliberately-corrupted parity; verify target ignores the transaction (or returns FAULT after a subsequent transaction); recover via line reset.
Request packet Start/Stop/Park — issue Request with Start=0 or Stop=1 or Park=0; verify target ignores (protocol error).
ACK code validation — for each transaction class, verify target returns one of OK=001 / WAIT=010 / FAULT=100; any other 3-bit pattern is a target compliance failure.
Data parity on read — verify the 33rd bit of every read = even parity of the 32 data bits.
Data parity on write — write 32-bit data with deliberately corrupted parity; verify CTRL/STAT.WDATAERR is set; subsequent transaction returns FAULT; clear via ABORT.WDERRCLR; retry.
Turnaround — verify 1-cycle Turnaround on default TRNCNT; set TRNCNT to 4 and verify 4-cycle Turnaround.
ABORT register — set a sticky error (e.g. write with bad parity), then write ABORT with the corresponding clear bit; verify CTRL/STAT shows the bit cleared.
SELECT register — write SELECT with APSEL=N, APBANKSEL=M; verify the next AP transaction targets AP[N] register window bank M.
RDBUFF posted-read recovery — issue 3 consecutive AP reads; verify the data of read N appears at the ACK of read N+1; the final read recovered via DP.RDBUFF.
AP IDR readback — for each implemented AP, verify IDR (offset 0xFC) returns a non-zero value identifying the AP type/designer.
AP BASE readback — for each MEM-AP, verify BASE (offset 0xF8) points to a 4 KB-aligned CoreSight ROM Table; walk the table and enumerate entries.
MEM-AP TAR + DRW round-trip — write a known value to a scratch RAM via DRW; read back via DRW; verify match.

MEM-AP auto-increment Single — set CSW.AddrInc=Single + CSW.Size=Word; write 4 words via 4 successive DRW writes with TAR set once; verify TAR auto-increments by 4 per transfer; the 4 system-bus addresses are TAR_initial, TAR_initial+4, TAR_initial+8, TAR_initial+12.
MEM-AP auto-increment Packed — set CSW.AddrInc=Packed + CSW.Size=Byte; verify multiple byte writes per DRW transfer; TAR increments by 1 per byte.
MEM-AP 4K wrap-around — set TAR near a 4 KB boundary with Single auto-increment; verify the auto-increment wraps within the 4 KB page (per ADIv5 spec; some IDR.SizeSupported variants).
WAIT retry — induce target busy (e.g. by issuing a slow AP transaction); verify host retries return WAIT until target completes; final OK confirms completion.
FAULT recovery — induce AP transfer error (e.g. write to a non-existent system-bus address); verify CTRL/STAT.STICKYERR set; FAULT returned; clear via ABORT.STKERRCLR; retry.

SWJ-DP JTAG-to-SWD selection — start in JTAG mode; drive ≥ 50 cycles TMS=1; shift 16-bit 0xE79E LSB-first on TMS; drive ≥ 50 cycles TMS=1; verify subsequent SWD transactions succeed (and JTAG TAP no longer responds).
SWJ-DP SWD-to-JTAG selection — start in SWD mode; drive ≥ 50 cycles SWDIO=1; shift 16-bit 0xE73C LSB-first on SWDIO; drive ≥ 50 cycles SWDIO=1; verify subsequent JTAG TAP transactions succeed.

Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) — line reset + JTAG-to-SWD sequence + TARGETSEL write with target A's TPARTNO+TINSTANCE; verify only target A acknowledges; switch to target B via line reset + TARGETSEL with B's ID.
CDBGPWRUPREQ / CSYSPWRUPREQ — write the bits in CTRL/STAT; verify CDBGPWRUPACK / CSYSPWRUPACK come back set.
DAPABORT — issue a long AP transaction; while it is in-flight write ABORT.DAPABORT=1; verify the AP transaction is cancelled and CTRL/STAT is consistent.
DHCSR halt — write DHCSR with C_HALT=1 + C_DEBUGEN=1 via MEM-AP; verify CPU halts (DHCSR.S_HALT=1 on readback).
DHCSR step — from halted state, write DHCSR with C_STEP=1 + C_HALT=0; verify CPU executes exactly one instruction.
CoreSight ROM Table walk — read MEM-AP.BASE; read the 4 KB ROM Table entries; for each present entry, follow the offset and read the component IDs (ROM Table format per CoreSight Arch Spec).
Cortex-M debug entry — verify the host can halt the CPU before its first user-code instruction (catch-on-reset) via DEMCR.VC_CORERESET.
Sticky overrun — issue many posted reads without RDBUFF flushes; verify STICKYORUN is set; clear via ABORT.ORUNERRCLR.
